title: Fill the Dots for the Most Uniform Substrings
src: MathWorks OA, IIT Bombay, 2026 (Software Engineer role). Coding question 3 of 3.
body:
You are given a string s of lowercase letters and dots (.). Replace every dot with any lowercase letter.

A substring is beautiful if all its characters are the same. Substrings are counted by position, so a block of L equal letters contains L(L+1)/2 beautiful substrings.

Return the largest possible number of beautiful substrings after replacing the dots.
out: One integer: the maximum number of beautiful substrings. It can exceed 2<sup>31</sup>.

samples.ex: aaab gives blocks of 3 and 1: 6 + 1 = 7. aabb gives 3 + 3 = 6, so 7 is best.
Turn every dot into a: abaaaab has blocks a, b, aaaa, b, giving 1 + 1 + 10 + 1 = 13. Extending the b blocks instead (e.g. abbbabb, 1 + 6 + 1 + 3 = 11) is worse.
